# Physical Attribute Computation


## Overview
Physical Attribute Computation generates secondary volumetric fields (such as velocity, size, or distance) from primary data (intensity, geometry, or segmentation) to enhance Direct Volume Rendering (DVR) or fluid simulation [G]. It differs from siblings like [Interior Voxelize](995-interior-voxelize.md) or [Box-filtering Density Estimation](5987-box-filtering-density-estimation.md) by computing derived physical properties rather than raw density or occupancy, and from [Multi-pattern Volumetric Construction via Voxel Multiplication](8874-multi-pattern-volumetric-construction-via-voxel-multiplicati.md) by focusing on attribute derivation rather than pattern composition [G].

## Shared principles
Builds on [Volumetric Attribute and Density Formation](6304-volumetric-attribute-and-density-formation.md).

## Subtopics

### [Velocity Voxelization](3082-velocity-voxelization.md)
Computes the instantaneous velocity of an obstacle at each grid cell containing part of the obstacle's boundary, producing a volumetric velocity field for fluid simulation. It differs from standard density voxelization by explicitly interpolating vertex velocities across triangle-slice intersections and rasterizing "thickened" segments (quads) to populate the velocity field, rather than merely counting coverage or depth. It is best suited for watertight closed meshes where front and back faces are distinct. See [Velocity Voxelization](3082-velocity-voxelization.md).

### [Size Volume Computation](9487-size-volume-computation.md)
Generates a tertiary volumetric attribute representing the characteristic size of local structures, used to drive transfer functions in Direct Volume Rendering (DVR). It addresses the difficulty of defining mathematical descriptors for size variations in multiscale fields. Unlike siblings that compute scalar intensity or velocity, this method categorizes objects by their spatial extent, allowing users to distinguish features based on scale rather than just value. See [Size Volume Computation](9487-size-volume-computation.md).

### Distance Attribute
#### definition
A volumetric attribute not directly derived from intensity, but calculated on pre-segmented parts of a volume [S1, unofficial]. It identifies regions close to a location of interest [S1, unofficial].
#### usage
Used to delimit spherical neighborhoods, such as layers adjacent to a tumor in a vascular dataset [S1, unofficial].

## Background
The concept of using attributes beyond intensity for visualization was explored in the context of transfer functions [G]. Tappenbeck, Preim, and Dicken (2006) introduced distance as a volumetric attribute calculated on pre-segmented parts to identify regions near a location of interest, such as delimiting spherical neighborhoods around a tumor [S1, unofficial]. Correa and Ma (2008) adapted the concept of "size" to Direct Volume Rendering, noting the difficulty in defining mathematical descriptors for size variations in multiscale fields, similar to challenges in Computer Vision .
